title: Trajectory playbook for Q2 hosted API + model lineup sprint anchoring
creator: Aisha Malik
project: Hosted API & Model Catalog Q2 Runway
description: Create a cross-functional playbook that anchors the quarterly sprint for Hosted API and model catalog convergence. The playbook will formalize decision gates, rollout lanes, capacity hedges, evaluation criteria, and stakeholder responsibilities. It focuses on minimizing user-facing regression risk during model rotations while enabling capacity-first scheduling and canary windows. Deliverables: 1) cadence calendar with commitment lanes and rollback triggers, 2) evaluation template linking evals to automated regression alerts, 3) acceptance criteria for canary windows and model substitutability matrix, 4) staffing/ops runbook for surge scenarios.
comments: 2026-03-02: Initial kickoff with Eng, Runtime, DX and SRE. Agreed on primary metric set: median p50 latency, 95th token latency, token cost delta, and customer error-rate by cohort. Action: ENG to surface current throughput envelopes by model family. (Jonah)

2026-03-04: Design reviewed proposed canary communications UI; raised question on per-route visibility in Console. Design to prototype a 'canary badge' and a quick link to sample prompts. (Riley Chen)

2026-03-06: ENG update: kernel scheduling improvements (ENG-1842) may change latency baseline — will provide revised thresholds by 2026-03-09. Blocker: need test fleet for staged traffic mirroring. (Marcos)

2026-03-09: PM sync: decoupled 'rotation anchor' from release window — will allow mid-window emergency swaps with stricter regression gate. Decided to require automated eval run + manual PM signoff for emergency swaps. (Aisha)
2026-03-11: Draft playbook posted to Confluence. Asked SRE to review the surge runbook and ops escalations. Next: align on on-call runbook and SLA degradation policies.
acceptance_criteria: Defined cadence calendar with named commitment lanes and canary windows published to Calendar
Canary evaluation template implemented and wired to regression alerting (automated eval -> alert)

Ops runbook includes step-by-step rollback, emergency-swap criteria, and stakeholder contact list
Stakeholder signoffs from Runtime, SRE, Design, and Legal for the playbook

decision_log: 2026-03-02: Adopted hybrid rollout model — capacity-first lanes with prioritized fallbacks rather than single global switch.
2026-03-09: Emergency swap path requires automated eval pass + manual PM signoff; removal of automatic fallback for top-tier accounts.
2026-03-10: Canary windows standardized at 48 hours for small rotations and 72 hours for model-family rotations unless waived.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Latency regressions after kernel swap. Mitigation: explicit p95/p99 thresholds, quick rollback scripts, and pre-swap dry-run on mirrored traffic.
Risk: Insufficient observability for per-route regressions. Mitigation: instrument per-route cost/latency panels and add tracer headers to test traffic.
Risk: Staff overload during peak rotation weeks. Mitigation: cross-train SRE on model operations and schedule dedicated on-call overlap.
